newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian shares firm, seen boosted by Lek.
newsitem.headline: Slovenian shares firm, seen boosted by Lek.

text.p: Slovenian shares rose 0.51 percent on Wednesday and traders said the market could climb higher, boosted by the strength of newly listed A issue of drugs company Lek.
"As long as Lek goes on rising on such large turnover, it could pull the whole market up further," one broker said.
Since it was listed two weeks ago, Lek's A issue have jumped 26.8 percent.
* The seven-share SBI index rose 4.69 points to 929.86.
* 14 shares rose and six fell, while four were untraded.
* Turnover eased to 216.6 million tolars from 259.7 million.
* Lek's A issue had the highest turnover, rising 5.13 percent to 17,455 tolars on volume of 12,031 shares for total turnover of 210 million tolars.
* Construction company GPG was the top gainer, rising 10 percent to 6,600 on volume of 313 shares for total turnover of 2.1 million tolars.
* Preferred shares of bank Dolenjska banka were the leading decliners. They fell 7.28 percent to 10,600 on volume of 15 shares for total turnover of 0.2 million tolars.

* Although warehousing company BTC today announced a decline in its half-year net profit, its shares rose 8.1 percent to 13,200 on volume of 35 shares for total turnover of 0.5 million tolars. -- Marja Novak, Ljubljana newsroom, 386-61-125-8439
